Quotes / Albert Camus / Q0108

There are more things to admire in men than to despise.
Thinker Albert Camus
School Philosophy of the Absurd

Theme Humanity
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with The Plague, within the tradition of Philosophy of the Absurd. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of humanity, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Albert Camus's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
